video_title: Is Micron Stock an Undervalued Stock to Buy? | MU Stock Analysis
summary:
Micron Technology is currently undervalued despite a massive stock price surge because the AI-driven data center boom and new long-term customer agreements have structurally transformed the company's profitability and revenue potential.

• Micron operates a capital-intensive business model by owning its manufacturing facilities in the U.S., Singapore, and Taiwan, which provides significant financial leverage and higher profit margins during periods of high demand.
• The company has experienced a structural shift where data centers have replaced PCs and smartphones as the primary revenue driver, creating a massive, permanent market for AI-optimized memory and storage solutions.
• Recent financial growth is driven primarily by extreme pricing power, with average selling prices for memory increasing by 260% and storage by 310% year-over-year, while unit shipments grew by only 10% to 20%.
• To mitigate traditional semiconductor cyclicality, Micron is entering strategic long-term agreements with customers that establish price floors and ceilings to ensure supply assurance and predictable financial performance.
• Management expects that even at the minimum floor pricing of these new agreements, gross profit margins will exceed the peak levels seen in any previous market cycle.
• The company's trailing 12-month revenue has reached $90 billion, which is triple its previous historical peak, while operating profit margins in the most recent quarter exceeded 80%.
• Despite the stock rising 240% in a single year, it trades at a low forward P/E of 6.4, and the speaker's valuation model suggests a fair value of $1,487 per share compared to the current $971 price.
